purpose: Canonical comparative dataset for intelligence, security and federal investigative organizations. It maps legal/public institutional identity, country, origin date, headquarters where publicly established, parent relationships and public functions. It does not infer covert relationships.
epistemic_rule: Public institutional facts are separated from allegations, intelligence claims and project interpretations. Unknown personnel counts are not estimated as active membership.

records.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation
records.note: The FBI traces its institutional origin to the Department of Justice special-agent force created in 1908; the name Federal Bureau of Investigation was adopted in 1935.

records.name: Central Intelligence Agency
records.note: Created by the National Security Act of 1947.

records.name: Mossad
records.note: Israel's Institute for Intelligence and Special Operations. Exact operational staffing and locations are not publicly disclosed.

records.name: Security Service (MI5)
records.note: Began as the Home Section of the Secret Service Bureau in 1909; the modern statutory name is Security Service.

records.name: Secret Intelligence Service (SIS / MI6)
records.note: Originated in the Foreign Section of the Secret Service Bureau in 1909.

records.name: National Security Agency
records.note: Established by presidential directive in 1952; exact historical legal lineage should be sourced separately.

records.name: National Reconnaissance Office
records.note: U.S. organization responsible for designing, acquiring and operating reconnaissance systems.

records.name: National Security Council
records.note: Policy-coordination institution rather than an intelligence collection agency.

records.name: Joint Intelligence Committee
records.note: UK intelligence assessment body within the Cabinet Office system.

counts_policy: Do not fabricate current headcounts for clandestine agencies. Where an official annual report supplies personnel counts, store the year and source as a time-series observation. For groups without reliable membership data, use estimated ranges only when a credible source provides one and label the estimate and methodology.
